overview: Palestine is the name for the Palestinian territories of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip. The State of Palestine is recognised by most members of the United Nations and has observer status there. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, Gaza has been devastated by war since 2023, and the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians remains unresolved. Arabic is the official language.

geography.text: The West Bank lies west of the Jordan River. It is mostly hilly, with the Jordan Valley and the shore of the Dead Sea along its eastern edge. The Gaza Strip is a small, flat and very densely populated strip of land on the Mediterranean coast, bordering Israel and Egypt.

history.text: The region has been home to many peoples and ruled by many empires over thousands of years. After Ottoman rule, Britain governed Palestine from 1920 to 1948. In the war of 1948 around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled, an event Palestinians call the Nakba. Israel occupied the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza in 1967. The Oslo Accords of the 1990s created the Palestinian Authority, but an independent Palestinian state has not been achieved.

events.title: The Nakba
events.text: Around 700,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled.

events.title: Occupation
events.text: Israel occupies the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza.

events.title: Oslo Accords
events.text: Israel and the PLO recognise each other.

events.title: UN observer state
events.text: The UN General Assembly recognises Palestine as a non-member observer state.

government.text: The State of Palestine is recognised by about 150 UN members. The Palestinian Authority, led by a President, governs parts of the West Bank under Israeli occupation. Hamas took control of Gaza in 2007. No national elections have been held since 2006. Palestine is a UN observer state.

economy.text: The Palestinian economy is heavily restricted by Israeli controls on movement, borders and trade. Many people depend on aid. The war in Gaza since 2023 has destroyed much of its economy, homes and infrastructure.

culture.text: Palestinian culture is famous for embroidery called tatreez, olive farming and food such as maqluba and knafeh. The keffiyeh scarf is a national symbol. Bethlehem, birthplace of Jesus in Christian tradition, and Hebron's old town are UNESCO sites.

items.title: Olive trees
items.text: Some trees are thought to be more than 1,000 years old.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Palestine's men's team was recognised by FIFA in 1998 and reached the knockout stage of the Asian Cup for the first time in 2024.

items.text: Reached the Asian Cup's round of 16 for the first time.

didYouKnow: Jericho is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, over 10,000 years old.
